text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat talked about Palestinian developments after Israel's decision to build a new settlement in Jerusalem.
- Mubarak has talks with Eritrean President Isayas Afewerki on Somalia, Sudan and the Great Lakes region.
- Mubarak will visit the New Valley project within hours.
- Mubarak will have talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Cairo on Wednesday.
- Mubarak and Arafat discuss the crisis over the settlement in Jerusalem. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says any geograghic or legal change in Jerusalem is invalid.
- The chief executive of Lehman Brothers has asked to see Mubarak during the president's visit to Washington next week.

- Abdel Shakour Shaalan of the International Monetary Fund said Egypt's budget deficit this year will be 0.8 percent (of gross domestic product). Mubarak will meet some IMF officials in Washington, he added.
- The Jordanian ambassador says there is no truth to reports that Jordan might sign a defence agreement with Israel.

- Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily leaves for Europe on Monday with Gamal Bayoumi, Egypt's negotiator in talks with the European Union on an association agreement. They will go to France, Germany, Italy and Holland. Bayoumi said they would meet ministers of foreign affairs, trade and agriculture to discuss finishing off the negotiations, especially on agricultural trade. Egypt will say it expects the European Union to reciprocate by liberalising agricultural imports from Egypt.
